item.title: High-Sensitivity Magnetometry with Scalable Mixed SQUID Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.26959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The utilisation of Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs), a loop of superconducting material hosting two Josephson junctions, has long been at the forefront of quantum sensing. To enhance performance and signal power, modern architectures connect multiple SQUIDs into two-dimensional series-parallel arrays called Superconducting Quantum Interference Filters (SQIFs). A major recent advancement, called a mixed-SQUID array, integrates junction-free ``bare" loops alongside active SQUID loops, offering a promising strategy to engineer high-performance alternatives to traditional SQIF technology. However, a rigorous theoretical optimization and performance scaling analysis for this novel geometry remains lacking. In this work, an analytical framework, validated against full numerical simulations, is developed to establish fundamental design rules for this technology. This work systematically examines how key quantum sensing parameters evolve as a function of loop inductance, parasitic coupling, and overall array dimensions. Crucially, it is demonstrated that these mixed SQUID arrays circumvent the severe inductive screening losses inherent to conventional SQIF designs, achieving a performance boost in flux sensitivity in the range of $2-4\:\times$ under realistic device parameters.
item.dc:creator: Anjishnu Bose, Jonathan Marenkovic, Giuseppe C. Tettamanzi

item.title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe2-xTex Polytypic Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.27220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure-superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2-xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range-from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T' structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8)shows suppressed Tc (~ 2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin-orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.
item.dc:creator: Xiangqi Liu, Haonan Wang, Ziguang Liu, Peihan Sun, Xiang Xu, Jing Jiang, Zhengyang Li, Ziyi Zhu, Wei Xia, Xia Wang, Leiming Chen, Ke Qu, Yulin Chen, Cheng Chen, Kai Liu, Zhenzhong Yang, Yanfeng Guo

item.title: Normal-state exponential muon-spin relaxation and its implications for time-reversal symmetry breaking in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-temperature increase of the zero-field muon-spin relaxation rate in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ has long been regarded as evidence for spontaneous internal fields associated with time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) superconductivity. Here we directly test this interpretation using muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements on high-quality Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ single crystals. For all four samples, the onset temperature of the additional exponential relaxation in the zero-field$\mu$SR data, $T_{\Lambda}$, lies below the bulk superconducting transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, even in the absence of applied strain. More importantly, in transverse-field $\mu$SR measurements we find a quantitatively similar exponential relaxation in a field of 80 mT applied along the crystallographic $c$ axis. This field exceeds the upper critical field of the crystals studied in transverse-field geometry and suppresses bulk superconductivity, demonstrating that the characteristic relaxation persists in the normal state. Measurements below the upper critical field reveal an additional superconducting mixed-state contribution superposed on this normal-state channel. Our results show that the zero-field $\mu$SR relaxation in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ cannot, by itself, be regarded as a unique signature of superconducting TRSB. They call for a reassessment of a key experimental signature of TRSB in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ and highlight the need to distinguish superconducting and normal-state relaxation channels in other unconventional superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Rustem Khasanov, Thomas J. Hicken, Jonas A. Krieger, Maxime Lamotte, Toni Shiroka, Jake S. Bobowski, Vadim Grinenko, Thomas Johnson, Naoki Kikugawa, Hans-Henning Klauss, Shubhankar Paul, Benjamin M. Huddart, Stephen J. Blundell, Hubertus Luetkens, Yoshiteru Maeno

item.title: Annular Terahertz Near-Field of a Breathing Charged Vortex
item.description: arXiv:2611.27532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the radial electric field around a singly quantized vortex in a charged BCS superconductor, when the Higgs amplitude mode is driven by a uniform terahertz (THz) electromagnetic pulse. In a local-density approximation the pairing gap vanishes on the vortex axis at all times, so the particle density on the axis cannot oscillate, whereas the curvature of the density profile around the axis does. Starting from the electrostatic-lens formalism of our previous work, we show that this converts the electrically neutral Higgs oscillation into an alternating radial electric field that vanishes on the axis. When the electrostatic screening length is much shorter than the vortex core, we obtain the field in closed form: it has a ring-shaped profile, with a maximum at a distance of the order of the coherence length from the axis, and the Higgs drive modulates it by a fraction $2\eta$, where $\eta$ is the relative oscillation of the gap. For niobium nitride and $\eta=0.1$ the static field of the vortex is about $140$~V/m and its modulation about $30$~V/m, independently of the carrier density and of the dielectric constant. We also discuss how the thermodynamic factor entering the field changes toward the BCS-BEC crossover.
item.dc:creator: I. Tolbatov, L. Salasnich

item.title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.
item.dc:creator: Matthew D. Thomson, Simon M. Martin, Frank Marsiglio, Joseph Maciejko

item.title: Atomic layer etching of niobium via alternating O$_2$ and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures
item.description: arXiv:2611.26735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Niobium thin films are a key component of superconducting detectors and electronics, and film surface quality, surface roughness, and geometrical dimensional accuracy affect many performance metrics. Atomic layer etching (ALE) is of interest for modifying film surfaces owing to its Angstrom-scale etching precision and surface smoothing characteristics. Here, we report a plasma-enhanced ALE process for Nb based on sequential O$_2$ plasma and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures. The process achieves an etch per cycle of 5-7 Angstrom/cycle and exhibits surface smoothing. The superconducting transition temperature of the ALE-treated films is maintained up to the expected decrease associated with reduced film thickness. Our ALE process could find applications in superconducting electronics for which surface quality and precise thickness control are of high importance.
item.dc:creator: Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Azmain A. Hossain, Yifei Yan, Austin J. Minnich

item.title: Lattice-geometry dependence of Type-I and Type-II magnetic flux responses in strongly correlated bosons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superfluids and superconductors are classified into Type-I and Type-II according to their response to a magnetic flux, but this classification has hardly been addressed for lattice bosons under magnetic flux, where the Meissner and vortex phases have been studied mostly in ladder geometries. Here, we study the flux response of the extended Bose-Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor interaction $V$ at half filling on square and triangular ladders with two to four legs by using the density-matrix renormalization group. On the square ladders, the vortex phase is confined to a region near $V=0$. At finite $V$, a magnetic flux-induced charge-density-wave (CDW) order replaces it, and the response becomes Type-I-like. In contrast, on the triangular ladders, the vortex phase persists over the whole range of $V$ studied, and the response remains Type-II-like. By extrapolating the ladder results to two dimensions, we argue that the Type-I or Type-II character of the flux response depends on the lattice geometry, which suggests a role of geometric frustration.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Yokoyama, Yasuhiro Tada

item.title: Quasiclassical theory of nonlinear response in d-wave superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2606.26909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent THz pump-probe experiments in unconventional superconductors, in this paper we use Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical theory of $d$-wave superconductors to analyze the third-harmonic generation. A systematic perturbative solution of the out-of-equilibrium Eilenberger equation for the Keldysh propagator is developed with respect to the amplitude of an external electromagnetic field. We show that in a clean superconductor and for a spatially uniform electromagnetic field third harmonic response is absent. In the presence of elastic impurity scattering which we treat using the self-consistent scattering matrix approximation in the Born limit we find that the third-harmonic current density is a sum of the Higgs (amplitude) mode and quasiparticle contributions. We compute their dependence on disorder, temperature, frequency and polarization of external radiation.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Steineman, Samuel Awelewa, Maxim Dzero

item.title: Ambient-pressure superconductivity in bulk single crystals of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconductivity in the Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelates has so far been confined either to multilayer compounds under high pressure or to square-planar infinite-layer-type films stabilized by epitaxial strain. Here, we report the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) growth of bulk single crystals of the quadruple-layer RP nickelate La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ ($n=4$) and reproduce the quintuple-layer La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{16}$ ($n=5$) synthesis, phases previously accessible only as thin films. Topotactic reduction of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ single crystals with CaH$_2$ yields the square-planar La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$, which we show to be a bulk, ambient-pressure superconductor with $T_\mathrm{c}^\mathrm{onset}\approx18.7$\,K, a shielding fraction above 60\%, and a specific-heat jump that confirms a bulk pairing transition. In transport, all crystals show an anomaly near 90~K reminiscent of a density-wave like transition, which may arise from a partially gapped Fermi surface or from the non-superconducting volume fraction. The upper critical field shows a small anisotropy, $\gamma \approx 2.4$, which remains finite as $T \to T_c$, indicating three-dimensional superconductivity with substantial coupling between the four-layer blocks. These results identify the square-planar nickelates $R_{n+1}$Ni$_n$O$_{2n+2}$ as a bulk platform in which the layer number alone tunes the nickel valence into the superconducting regime, without chemical substitution, pressure, or epitaxial constraint.
item.dc:creator: R. Zhang, P. Reiss, A. Krajewska, M. Isobe, H. Takagi, P. Puphal

item.title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
item.description: arXiv:2611.25456v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe M\"ossbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.
item.dc:creator: A. G. Gavriliuk, I. A. Troyan, A. A. Mironovich, A. G. Ivanova, H. -K. Mao, V. V. Struzhkin

item.title: Mitigating transients in flux-control signals in a superconducting quantum processor
item.description: arXiv:2503.08645v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Flux-tunable qubits and couplers are common components in superconducting quantum processors. However, dynamically controlling these elements via current pulses poses challenges due to distortions and transients in the propagating signals. In particular, long-time transients can persist, adversely affecting subsequent qubit control operations. We model the flux control line as a first-order RC circuit and introduce a class of pulses designed to mitigate long-time transients. We theoretically demonstrate the robustness of these pulses against parameter mischaracterization and provide experimental evidence of their effectiveness in mitigating transients when applied to a flux-tunable qubit coupler. The proposed pulse design offers a practical solution for mitigating long-time transients, enabling efficient and reliable experiment tune-ups without requiring detailed flux line characterization.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Aggarwal, Jorge Fern\'andez-Pend\'as, Tahereh Abad, Daryoush Shiri, Halld\'or Jakobsson, Marcus Rommel, Andreas Nylander, Emil Hogedal, Amr Osman, Janka Bizn\'arov\'a, Robert Rehammar, Michele Faucci Giannelli, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, Jonas Bylander, Giovanna Tancredi

item.title: Electronic structure, quasiparticle renormalizations, and magnetic correlations in the alternating single-layer bilayer nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$
item.description: arXiv:2604.26627v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using DFT+DMFT we study the electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$ (1212-LNO). Our results exhibit qualitative differences for the structurally distinct single-layer and bilayer Ni ions, implying the importance of confinement and orbital-dependent correlations. The Ni $e_g$ states originating from the bilayer Ni ions form strongly renormalized quasiparticle bands with a large enhancement factor $m^*/m \sim 3.5$ and 4.2 for the Ni $x^2-y^2$ and $3z^2-r^2$ orbitals. Moreover, the $e_g$ states of the single-layer Ni ions exhibit an orbital-selective Mott insulating state, with a narrow energy gap for the Ni $3z^2-r^2$ states and metallic, strongly non-Fermi-liquid Ni $x^2-y^2$ ones. Our analysis of magnetic correlations suggests the formation of intertwined spin and charge density wave stripes in the bilayer NiO$_6$ slab, in close similarity to the double-layer material. We identify two major instabilities: a leading one associated with a propagating wave vector ${\bf Q}=(\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ ("up-down-0" spin pattern or "$d^8$-$d^8$-$d^8\underline{L}$'' charge-density wave with Ni $d^8\underline{L}$ ions bonded in an interlayer spin polaron), competing with $(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{4})$ ("up-up-down-down") stripe state. The single-layer Ni $3d$ electrons exhibit an instability toward the N\'eel magnetic state. Under pressure, 1212-LNO undergoes an orbital-selective Mott insulator-to-metal transition, associated with metallization of the single-layer Ni $e_g$ states. The single-layer Ni $e_g$ bands exhibit non-Fermi-liquid behavior with strongly incoherent spectral weights near $E_F$. We note that correlation effects result in a crossover from single-layer (as obtained within DFT) to double-layer dominated magnetic correlations.
item.dc:creator: I. V. Leonov

item.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
item.description: arXiv:2609.16320v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{\mu eV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. The local density of states remains suppressed over distances exceeding $1\,\mu$m. Our results demonstrate the potential of BLG-superconductor hybrids as a tunable platform combining QDs and quantum point contacts with superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Schmidt, Mathies Funke, Till Tenger, Katarina Stanojevi\'c, Hubert Dulisch, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Fabian Hassler, Christian Volk, Szabolcs Csonka, Christoph Stampfer
